claim: Session key derived from event_id prefix (trailing -N stripped), not the documented connection_id field
proves: connection_id alternates between two forms within a single real session across all 62,515 sessions checked
does_not_prove: that this key format is stable for a hidden fixture with different identifiers
alternative_considered: connection_id + source_ip + protocol + sensor_time (documented key) -- rejected, splits every session

claim: Public fixture P-SESSION-01 requires splitting a session on connect-after-disconnect even within one event_id-prefix group
proves: session_count=2 is required for 6 events sharing one prefix
does_not_prove: that this pattern occurs in the sealed replay itself (verified separately, see E-004)
alternative_considered: treat shared prefix as always = 1 session -- disproven directly by this fixture
disposition: adopted, implemented in sessionizer.py, verified by all 16/16 fixtures passing

claim: Full 250,000-event sealed replay produces 62515 sessions with exact accounting (no events lost or double-counted)
proves: 250000 raw events consumed = 250,000 raw lines (see reconciliation.json)
does_not_prove: correctness of session BOUNDARIES, only that no events were dropped/duplicated in aggregate

claim: Every raw line in honeypot-replay.jsonl is accounted for as either clean or quarantined, with zero malformed rows in this dataset
does_not_prove: that the quarantine logic works on malformed input -- this dataset never exercises it (see decision-log.md D-014)

claim: 3 IPs (198.51.100.155, 198.51.100.160, 198.51.100.87) jointly delivered 4 distinct payload hashes
proves: these 3 IPs functioned as shared delivery infrastructure for 4 distinct payloads
does_not_prove: common actor identity or intent -- only that identical binary content across multiple samples was distributed via this consistent IP set
alternative_considered: treating each payload hash as a separate cluster -- rejected per D-009, understated the finding

claim: Credential-overlap across 251 IPs is statistically consistent with independent sampling from a shared wordlist, not shared attacker infrastructure
proves: sampled pairwise overlap (28-35) closely matches chance-expected overlap (~28.9 = n1*n2/N)
does_not_prove: that no relationship exists between any two IPs -- only that overlap alone can't distinguish one
alternative_considered: cluster IPs by any shared credential (threshold=1) and threshold=3 -- both collapsed to one 251-IP mega-cluster, rejected as meaningless
disposition: reported as aggregate note, not used as a clustering mechanism (D-008)

claim: stix-bundle.json contains 19 valid STIX 2.1 objects, round-trip parsed successfully
proves: all objects satisfy STIX 2.1 required-property and id-format rules (stix2 library construction/parse)
does_not_prove: pass against stix2-validator CLI tool, which failed due to a documented tooling schema-availability gap (D-011), not a bundle defect
alternative_considered: stix2-validator CLI -- attempted, failed for tooling reasons, documented in D-011
disposition: verified via stix2.parse(), object type counts, and manual content inspection

claim: Recon-command Sigma rule matches 293 real sessions containing the exact command 'uname -a && id' (verification re-confirmed and timestamped 2026-08-01T08:37:58Z; original check run earlier in session, exact original time not separately logged)
proves: the rule's detection logic fires on real true positives present in this dataset
does_not_prove: generalization to other recon commands not in this exact form
alternative_considered: N/A -- direct count verification against real data
disposition: verified, rule converts cleanly via pySigma/Elasticsearch backend

report_section: Detection content validation (negative finding, by design)
claim: Credential-stuffing correlation rule (10m window, >=5 threshold) will not meaningfully trigger against this project's honeypot capture
proves: 248 IPs show uniform low-and-slow behavior (median 247 attempts, ~0.09/min), max 3 events in any 1-min window -- no volume/burst outlier exists at any tested window size
does_not_prove: that this rule is broken -- it's designed for production deployment where a benign baseline exists to separate against, which a honeypot's 100%-malicious population does not have
alternative_considered: lowering threshold to force a match against this dataset -- rejected, would produce a rule with no discriminating power in real deployment
disposition: kept as production-oriented detection, explicitly documented as not expected to fire here

claim: 4 distinct payload hashes identified and quarantined by hash/metadata only, never executed
proves: every payload_download event's hash traces to a real session with locators
does_not_prove: the actual content/behavior of the payloads (deliberately not examined, per the never-execute safety rule)
disposition: verified against clusters.json cross-check (same 3 IPs, same 4 hashes)
